round2.resolved_by: Claude (Anthropic), fixer group G3, 18 Oct 2026 (review round 2); pending team review

accepted.change: Reproduced and fixed as suggested. With the rectangular window (n = 9600 at 48 kHz, 5 Hz bins) an IF off the bin grid leaks power outside 1.9-2.1 kHz: reviewer files lo_freq 8699 / 8701 / 8697.5 gave 0.996593 / 0.99659 / 0.990093 and failed V6, although the instruction allows 2 kHz within 1 %. The band_fraction check now carries "window": "blackman" (tooling T5; build.py BF_WINDOW). Re-run of the reviewer's own files against the version-3 task.json: 8690, 8697.5, 8699, 8701 and 8710 all pass with band_fraction 1.0. build.py --probes (new) adds lo_freq 8699, 8701, 8682 (IF 2018 Hz, +0.9 %), 8718 (1982 Hz, -0.9 %), 12718 (high side, 2018 Hz), 8690 and 8710: all pass with 1.0. Valid alternatives the reviewer showed are kept as a variant (rule R10): v5_lo_within_tolerance, lo_freq 8697.5 (IF 2002.5 Hz, half a bin off the grid, the worst case for the old check), which passes the gates. The window does not weaken the kill side: in the probe run, the bypassed-LPF mutant gives 0.5 and the 18.8 kHz near-miss cutoff 0.999783 (sum product 36.6 dB down, < 0.9999). Both still fail, and the gates kill 13/13 mutants. A window scales every tone's power by the same factor, so the fraction still measures the stated 40 dB power ratio (threshold 0.9999 unchanged). Updated: spec_properties.sum_product_removed.checked_by, the build.py calibration paragraph (the old 'every tone on an FFT bin, no leakage' rationale is replaced), and review.notes limit (4) (the purity requirement is measured as power outside +-100 Hz of 2 kHz). The probes also reproduce the round-1 claims: the two 2 kHz-tone shortcuts fail only the mixer-structure graph checks, and the start with lo_freq = 0 passes p2p and fails f2p.
